lead: The 123.38M minKron decoder trains stably within this CPU allocation, but 25 minutes buys only 134,144 training targets. It learns common words and short patterns; the ten samples are not coherent prose.
thoughts: The model is learning rather than merely producing random vocabulary. Development NLL fell from 10.9841 to 7.2686 on the same 8,192 targets. The untouched confirmation slice scored 7.2867, versus 7.8279 for an add-one unigram baseline fitted to the exact targets seen during training. The latter comparison is evidence of predictive learning beyond simple token frequencies, not evidence of useful reasoning or knowledge.

The generations show recognizable words, punctuation, and fragments such as “a lot” and “you can be.” They also show fused token fragments, repeated function words, broken agreement, and abrupt formatting changes. The continuations do not maintain the prompts’ topics. None of the ten supports a claim of reliable sentence-level composition.

Recurrent history contributes a measurable but modest benefit: clearing it before every token increases NLL by 0.1129 nats on a fixed 2,048-target diagnostic. That is consistent with some local context use. This test does not establish long-range memory, and training windows were only 256 tokens.

The systems result is more encouraging than the prose quality. The model fits in 4.40 GiB peak process RAM, carries only 144 KiB of recurrent state per sequence, and generates about 31.1 tokens/s at batch one. The complete training loop averages 89.4 targets/s. Small recurrent state does not remove the cost of dense weights, gradients, AdamW moments, logits, and BPTT activations.

The initial 203.4-target/s systems probe was optimistic for trained weights: 65.1% of chunk calls in the main run used the original numerically safe fallback. Reducing that fallback cost is the clearest next implementation target suggested by this run. Any per-head or fused alternative should retain the same output, state, and gradient checks.

My assessment: this is a successful scale and stability check, and a severely undertrained language model. The run used about 0.00109 training targets per parameter. More parameter capacity cannot compensate for that tiny amount of text. I would spend the next experiment on much more training data and a matched-budget comparator before judging minKron as an architecture; these ten samples do not establish its eventual quality.
